slice.name: delayed_duplicate_after_intervening_event_restart_reconstruction
slice.purpose: Extend the existing framed-journal idempotency leaf by accepting one distinct event e5 after e4b, simulating another process restart, reconstructing the applied-event index from the two validated durable frames, then replaying the older e4b frame after the intervening event.
slice.canonicalization: UTF-8 canonical JSON with sorted keys and separators ',' ':'; event payload digest is SHA-256 of canonical event JSON; commit digest is SHA-256 of canonical body {event,event_payload_digest,prev_chain}; complete frame adds commit_digest and one trailing newline.
slice.tested_scope: Deterministic small text state; exactly two complete sequential journal frames e4b then e5; one simulated restart after e5; reconstruction of the relevant two-entry applied-event index from those validated frames; and one delayed replay of the older e4b frame. This tests delayed duplicate recognition after one intervening accepted event. It does not establish arbitrarily long/corrupted journals, duplicate-ID payload conflicts, journal truncation/partial-tail recovery, compaction/tombstones, concurrent writers, lock-free progress, fairness, semantic model-weight adaptation, or indefinite repository availability.

zero_dependency_assessment.transport_note: All state transition, canonicalization, integrity calculation, restart reconstruction and replay checks were performed within the scheduled Chat invocation. Repository contents API is used only as lightweight durable transport/readback. The tested mechanism does not require a hosted runner, Codespaces, artifacts/LFS/packages, cloud credits, external model/API credits, protected authority, manual user execution, scheduler mutation, or incremental monetary cost.

slice.conflict_check: Only current sanitized controls, own role-local clean state and current-invocation computation were used. No O/O-derived, downstream, other-worker, shared-ledger, other-role receipt/config or legacy semantic input was consumed; no protected-primary or scheduler mutation occurred.

exact_continuation: Next invocation: stay on this single idempotency/restart leaf and test duplicate-ID payload conflict after restart. Starting from the validated two-frame e4b->e5 journal and reconstructed index, submit a frame whose event_id is e4b but whose patch payload differs from the stored e4b digest. Verify the event-id lookup occurs before prev_chain acceptance, returns an explicit duplicate_id_payload_conflict rejection rather than noop or apply, leaves post-e5 state/chain unchanged, and preserves all preexisting keys. Persist only that conflict evidence; do not start another leaf.
